verses.text: The LORD says, “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house could you build for me? Where could I rest?
My hand made all of this. That’s how everything came to be,” says the LORD. “Here’s the one I’ll look to: the poor person whose spirit is humbled and who trembles at my word.

Someone who kills an ox is like someone who kills a person. Someone who sacrifices a lamb is like someone who breaks a dog’s neck. Someone who brings an offering is like someone offering pig’s blood. Someone who burns frankincense is like someone who blesses an idol. They’ve chosen to do things their way, and they love the disgusting things they do.

So I’ll choose their delusions and bring the very things they fear on them. I called and nobody answered. I spoke and they didn’t listen. They did what was evil in my eyes and chose what gave me no joy.”

Hear the LORD’s word, you who tremble at what he says. “Your own brothers hate you and threw you out because of my name. They said, ‘Let the LORD be glorified so we can see your joy.’ They’re the ones who’ll end up ashamed.
Hear the uproar from the city! Hear the voice from the temple! It’s the LORD’s voice giving his enemies what they deserve.
“Before she went into labor, she gave birth. Before the pains came, she delivered a son.

Who’s ever heard of such a thing? Who’s ever seen anything like it? Can a land be born in a day? Can a whole nation come into being all at once? The moment Zion went into labor, she gave birth to her children.
Would I bring a child to the moment of birth and then hold back the delivery?” says the LORD. “Would I, the one who makes birth happen, close the womb?” says your God.
“Celebrate with Jerusalem. Be glad for her, all of you who love her. Celebrate right along with her, all you who’ve mourned over her.
Then you can nurse until you’re satisfied at her comforting breasts. You can drink deeply and delight in how full of glory she is.”
The LORD says, “Look, I’ll send peace flowing to her like a river and the glory of nations like a stream overflowing its banks. You’ll nurse. You’ll be carried at her side and bounced on her knees.
I’ll comfort you like a mother comforts her child. You’ll find comfort in Jerusalem.”
You’ll see it, and your hearts will be glad. Your bones will grow strong like tender grass. The LORD will show his hand to his servants and his anger to his enemies.
Look, the LORD will come with fire. His chariots will roar in like a whirlwind. He’ll let loose his fierce anger and deliver his rebuke in flames.
The LORD will judge all humanity with fire and with his sword. Many will be killed by the LORD.

“People set themselves apart and make themselves clean to go into the gardens. They follow the one in the middle and eat pork, disgusting things, and mice. They’ll all come to an end together,” says the LORD.
“I know what they do and what they think. The time is coming when I’ll bring together all nations and languages. They’ll come and see my glory.

“I’ll set a sign among them and send the survivors to the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan and distant islands that haven’t heard of me or seen my glory. They’ll tell the nations about my glory.

They’ll bring all your brothers and sisters out of every nation as an offering to the LORD, on horses, in chariots and covered stretchers, on mules and camels, to my holy mountain, Jerusalem,” says the LORD. “It’ll be like the people of Israel bringing their offering into the LORD’s house in a clean container.
I’ll choose some of them as priests and Levites too,” says the LORD.
“The new heavens and the new earth I’ll make will stay before me,” says the LORD. “That’s how your descendants and your name will last.
From one new moon to the next, and from one Sabbath to the next, all humanity will come to worship before me,” says the LORD.
“They’ll go out and see the dead bodies of the people who rebelled against me. The worms feeding on them won’t die, their fire won’t go out, and all humanity will find them repulsive.”
